args.name: json
args.help: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of human output. `priority` and `type` carry canonical keys (stable ordinals / declared type keys), not display labels; the labels are available via `nxf schema` and, on `show`/`list`/`next`, the additive `priority_label`/`type_label` fields. `create`/`update` accept either the key or the label

args.name: db
args.help: Use this sqlite db file directly instead of discovering `.nxs/`

subcommands.name: agent-manifest
subcommands.about: Emit nxf's declared contribution to the shared agent file (the AGENTS.md section, the prime command, the SessionStart hook) as data. The `nxs` umbrella assembles the shared files from each active module's manifest; `--json` is the machine contract

subcommands.name: archive
subcommands.about: Archive one or more items — "closed and put away". Cascades DOWN: each root and its whole `belongs_to` subtree are archived, but only when the root is closed and every descendant is closed (already-archived counts as closed). Atomic per root, independent between roots; the result reports each root's outcome plus the full list of ids actually archived (incl. cascaded). Archiving is reversible — see `unarchive`

args.name: ids
args.help: Item ids to archive (each a cascade root). At least one is required

subcommands.name: archived
subcommands.about: List archived items (any status). Ordered by archive-date descending (most recent first); override with `--sort`

args.name: sort
args.help: Sort order: `archived` | `id` | `rank` (default `archived`). An unknown key is a loud error

subcommands.name: blocked
subcommands.about: List blocked items (open, with an open blocker or in a cycle). Ranked by default; override with `--sort id`

args.name: sort
args.help: Sort order: `rank` | `id` (default `rank`). An unknown key is a loud error

subcommands.name: claim
subcommands.about: Claim an item: mark it in progress (and optionally assign it)

args.name: id
args.help: Item id

args.name: assignee
args.help: Assignee to record

subcommands.name: close
subcommands.about: Close an item, recording why. Closing is final (no hard delete), so a reason is required

args.name: id
args.help: Item id

args.name: reason
args.help: Closing comment — required: why this item is being closed. `-` reads it from STDIN

args.name: reason_file
args.help: Read the closing comment from this file (UTF-8, verbatim); `-` reads STDIN. Mutually exclusive with `--reason`

subcommands.name: closed
subcommands.about: List closed items (excluding archived). Ordered by close-date descending (most recent first); override with `--sort`

args.name: sort
args.help: Sort order: `closed` | `id` | `rank` (default `closed`). An unknown key is a loud error

subcommands.name: contributes
subcommands.about: Add, remove, or list contributes-to edges: `from` contributes to `to` (n:m). Like a mention it never blocks — it records a structural "feeds into" relation, not a dependency

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.about: Record that `from` contributes to `to` (both must exist; never blocks)

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List the items `id` contributes to

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.about: Remove the `from -> to` contributes-to edge

subcommands.name: create
subcommands.about: Create a new item — a complete item in one call. Title, description, and priority are required; design, the definition of done, a parent, and dependencies are optional. Run `nxf schema` for the active plugin's field model (labels, constraints, required fields)

args.name: ty
args.help: Item type, from the active plugin's own vocabulary (under `issue-tracker`: `epic`, `feature`, `bug`, `chore`, `decision`). The set is plugin-declared, so run `nxf schema` for the one this workspace actually accepts

args.name: title
args.help: Item title (required)

args.name: description
args.help: Description — why this item exists and its goal (required). Pass `-` to read it from STDIN (escaping-free, multi-line; e.g. `cat desc.md | nxf create … --description -`), or supply it via `--description-file` instead

args.name: description_file
args.help: Read the description from this file (UTF-8, verbatim); `-` reads STDIN. Mutually exclusive with `--description`

args.name: priority
args.help: Priority — the plugin's named variant (e.g. P0..P4) OR its canonical ordinal key (0..4, the form `--json` emits), required; run `nxs prime`/`nxf schema` to see the set. Validated against it; ranks `next` by the variant order

args.name: design
args.help: Design — the path to the goal; can be filled in later (optional). `-` reads it from STDIN

args.name: design_file
args.help: Read the design from this file (UTF-8, verbatim); `-` reads STDIN

args.name: dod
args.help: Definition of done — what "done" means for this item (optional). `-` reads it from STDIN

args.name: dod_file
args.help: Read the definition of done from this file (UTF-8, verbatim); `-` reads STDIN

args.name: due
args.help: Due date (ISO-8601 / RFC3339)

args.name: defer
args.help: Defer-until date (ISO-8601 / RFC3339)

args.name: parent
args.help: Parent item id (sets belongs-to); must exist

args.name: depends_on
args.help: This item depends on <id> (repeatable): <id> must exist and blocks this item until it closes. Same direction as `dep add <this> <id>`

args.name: set
args.help: Set a plugin CUSTOM field: `name=value` (repeatable). Canonical fields use their own flags above; `--set` carries the active plugin's declared custom fields (run `nxf schema` for the set). Validated against the field's type; a value of `-` reads STDIN

args.name: set_file
args.help: Set a custom field from a file: `name=path` (UTF-8, verbatim); `path` of `-` reads STDIN. Repeatable. A field may be set by `--set` or `--set-file`, not both

args.name: id_only
args.help: Print ONLY the new item's id — one line, no JSON, no output framing — so it can be captured straight into the next command (`id=$(nxf create … -q)`) without parsing JSON. Takes precedence over `--json` (the id wins; `--json` is ignored, not an error)

args.name: json_stdin
args.help: `-` reads the whole item as one JSON object from STDIN (every field in one piped payload — no escaping, no flag combinatorics; pair with `--json` for JSON output too, the canonical form `nxf create --json -`). The only accepted value is `-`, and it is mutually exclusive with the field flags

subcommands.name: deferred
subcommands.about: List deferred items (open, unblocked, with a future defer date) — the lane that is neither ready nor blocked. Ordered by defer-date ascending (soonest first); override with `--sort`

args.name: now
args.help: Reference time (ISO-8601 / RFC3339); defaults to now. Sets the defer boundary

args.name: sort
args.help: Sort order: `defer` | `id` | `rank` (default `defer`). An unknown key is a loud error

subcommands.name: dep
subcommands.about: Add or remove a dependency edge. Direction: `dep add A B` makes A depend on B, so B blocks A — A cannot be ready until B closes

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.about: Make `from` depend on `to`: `to` blocks `from`, so `from` stays blocked until `to` closes. Rejected if it would create a cycle

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.about: Remove the dependency where `from` depends on `to`

subcommands.name: guide
subcommands.about: Print an embedded, offline guide. Omit the topic to list the available ones

args.name: topic
args.help: Guide topic; omit to list topics

subcommands.name: init
subcommands.about: Initialize a `.nxs` workspace in the current directory: set up flow, then delegate the shared agent file + one SessionStart hook per active module to the `nxs` assembler. To set up the whole suite (and pick tools interactively), use `nxs init` instead

args.name: plugin
args.help: Plugin to activate (vocabulary + ranking): `issue-tracker` | `personal-todo`. Required when non-interactive (`--json`/piped/`--quiet`); on a TTY, omitting it prompts

args.name: quiet
args.help: Driven/quiet mode: set up the workspace and delegate the agent files + the SessionStart hooks, but render no banner or prompt. The seam the `nxs` umbrella uses to drive `nxf init` without its output bleeding through; implies a non-interactive plugin choice (`--plugin`)

args.name: from_beads
args.help: Consent to the beads → nxs migration: in a project that still uses beads, import its tickets + memories and roll back beads' config. Routed through the `nxs` umbrella, which owns the migration

subcommands.name: label
subcommands.about: Add, remove, or list user labels (free-text tags) on an item. A label is user vocabulary, distinct from the plugin's display type; filter `list`/`next` with `--label`

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.about: Attach a label to an item (idempotent). The label is trimmed; a blank label is rejected

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List an item's labels (sorted)

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.about: Detach a label from an item (observed-remove)

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List items, optionally filtered by status and/or type. Id-ordered by default (so the `--json` record stays plugin-independent); override with `--sort rank`

args.name: status
args.help: Filter by status

args.name: ty
args.help: Filter by type, using the active plugin's vocabulary (see `nxf schema`)

args.name: label
args.help: Filter to items carrying this label (user vocabulary, not the display type)

args.name: sort
args.help: Sort order: `rank` | `id` (default `id`). An unknown key is a loud error

subcommands.name: mention
subcommands.about: Add, remove, or list reference edges (free-text short-id citations)

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.about: Record that `from` cites the short-id `to` in its free text (no blocking)

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List the short-ids `id` mentions

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.about: Remove the `from -> to` reference

subcommands.name: next
subcommands.about: List actionable work — ready plus already-claimed, unblocked, not deferred — ranked by the active plugin's `next` policy and tiered to finish before starting: work you can close now, then each started epic with its open children, then the backlog. `--sort id` gives the flat, untiered order; `--limit` shows only the head of it, and says so

args.name: now
args.help: Reference time (ISO-8601 / RFC3339); defaults to now

args.name: label
args.help: Filter to ready items carrying this label (user vocabulary, not the display type)

args.name: sort
args.help: Sort order: `rank` | `id` (default `rank`). An unknown key is a loud error

args.name: limit
args.help: Max items to show (default: no limit). Applied last — after `--sort` and `--label` — and never silently: a truncated list is headed `showing <n> of <total>`, and under `--json` the flag wraps the records as `{"items": [...], "total": <n>}` so a consumer reads the untruncated total instead of inferring it from the array's length

subcommands.name: note
subcommands.about: Add or list notes (the change/worklog stream) on an item

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.about: Append a note to an item. Pass `-` as the text to read the note body from STDIN (escaping-free, multi-line)

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List an item's notes

subcommands.name: recap
subcommands.about: Recap the most recently closed work — "what got finished lately" — newest close first, archived closes INCLUDED. A recency recall view, distinct from `closed` (the lane, which drops archived). `--limit` caps the count (default 10); `--since` keeps only later closes

args.name: limit
args.help: Max items to show (default 10)

args.name: since
args.help: Only closes on/after this ISO-8601 date (`YYYY-MM-DD` or RFC3339); filters `closed_at >= since`

subcommands.name: schema
subcommands.about: Describe the active plugin's field model — vocabulary, priorities, and per field whether it is required on create / settable on update and how. `--json` is the machine contract; run it to learn what `create`/`update` accept in this workspace (the static `--help` cannot carry the active plugin's vocabulary)

subcommands.name: search
subcommands.about: Search items by substring over title, description, design, DoD, and notes. Results are grouped by lane priority (next+in-progress → blocked → deferred → closed), each group in its natural order; archived items are excluded by default

args.name: query
args.help: Query string

args.name: status
args.help: Filter by status

args.name: ty
args.help: Filter by type, using the active plugin's vocabulary (see `nxf schema`)

args.name: now
args.help: Reference time (ISO-8601 / RFC3339); defaults to now. Sets the defer boundary used to group deferred matches

args.name: include_archived
args.help: Append the archived group (lowest priority) instead of excluding it

args.name: archived_only
args.help: Search ONLY the archive; the live lanes are skipped

args.name: sort
args.help: Flatten the lane grouping into one order by this key (`rank` | `id` | …). Unknown = loud error

subcommands.name: setup
subcommands.about: Wire host-specific agent integration (idempotent, merge-only). `nxf init` stays tool-agnostic; this opts a project into a host's deterministic delivery

subcommands.name: claude
subcommands.about: Wire Claude Code: (re)assemble the shared agent file (AGENTS.md) and one SessionStart hook per active module (`nxf prime`, `nxm prime`, `nxc prime`) plus the `nxs`/module permission allowlist, merged into `.claude/settings.json` (idempotent, never overwriting). The canonical verb is `nxs setup claude`; this delegates to it (host setup is an umbrella responsibility)

subcommands.name: show
subcommands.about: Show one item with its dependencies and notes

args.name: id
args.help: Item id

subcommands.name: thread
subcommands.about: Link a chat thread to a board item, or list what a thread is about. This is how the conversation that did the work and the ticket it was about stop being two artefacts: a later reader of the item sees that there are conversations, without having to go looking

subcommands.name: link
subcommands.about: Link `thread` to `item`. Re-running with different attributes UPDATES the link rather than adding a second one — that is how a link firms up once a passing mention turns out to be the subject

args.name: thread
args.help: The chat thread's own id. Not resolved or shape-checked: the thread lives in the chat store's id space, which flow holds the address of but does not own

args.name: item
args.help: The board item

args.name: relation
args.help: What the link consists in: `worked_on` (this thread is working on the item) or `cited` (it refers to the item without working on it). Default `worked_on` — the deterministic case, the one a work order's ticket set produces with no judgement involved

args.name: weight
args.help: How much the thread is about the item: `bearing` (the item is its subject) or `passing` (it came up, no more). Default `bearing`. Only `bearing` links are advertised by `next`; a `passing` one shows on the item itself, so a wandering conversation cannot flood the work list with items it merely touched

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List the board items `thread` is linked to

subcommands.name: unlink
subcommands.about: Unlink `thread` from `item`, whatever attributes the link currently carries

subcommands.name: unarchive
subcommands.about: Unarchive one or more items, making them visible again. Cascades UP only: each item and its ancestor chain resurface, but its children/siblings stay archived. Partial per root; the result reports each root's outcome plus the full list of ids actually unarchived

args.name: ids
args.help: Item ids to unarchive (each surfaces its ancestor chain). At least one is required

subcommands.name: update
subcommands.about: Update item fields via `--set field=value` (repeatable). The long-form `description`/`design`/`completion_criterion` are ordinary `--set` fields. Run `nxf schema` for the settable fields and their plugin names. Convention: correct the field model once shortly after creation; once it is stable, record what you learn as append-only notes (`nxf note add`) rather than further field edits

args.name: id
args.help: Item id

args.name: json_stdin
args.help: `-` reads the fields to set as one JSON object from STDIN (`{"description":"…", "design":"…"}`) — every field in one piped payload, no escaping. The only accepted value is `-` (canonical form `nxf update <id> --json -`), mutually exclusive with `--set`/`--set-file`

args.name: set
args.help: A `field=value` assignment; repeat for multiple fields. An unknown field is rejected with the settable set listed. Aliases (same words `create` uses): `parent`→belongs_to, `defer`→defer_until. A value of `-` reads that field from STDIN (escaping-free, multi-line); at most one field per call may read STDIN

args.name: set_file
args.help: A `field=path` assignment that reads the field's value from a file (UTF-8, verbatim); `path` of `-` reads STDIN. Repeatable; lets several long-text fields each come from their own file in one call. A field may be set by `--set` or `--set-file`, not both
